---
title: Range requests respect client Accept-Encoding
description: Uncached HTTPS GET range requests now forward the client's Accept-Encoding header, and cached encoded ranges go only to clients that accept the encoding.
products:
  - cache
date: 2026-11-24
---

Cloudflare updated how range requests handle content encoding for both cached files and uncached `GET` requests over HTTPS.

## Cached encoded files

A byte range of a cached file encoded with gzip or Brotli (`br`) counts bytes of the encoded file, not of the decompressed content ([RFC 9110, section 14.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-14.1.2)). Cloudflare now serves that range only if the client's `Accept-Encoding` header explicitly lists the encoding without `q=0` (and over HTTPS for Brotli). Otherwise, Cloudflare ignores `Range` ([RFC 9110, section 14.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-14.2)) and sends the complete file as `200 OK` using normal content negotiation. Cloudflare always sends the complete `200 OK` file for a cached file encoded with Zstandard (`zstd`) or `deflate`.

Previously, a client that did not accept the encoding could receive a `206 Partial Content` response whose bytes did not match its `Content-Range` header.

## Uncached range requests

If caching is bypassed or the request is not eligible for caching, Cloudflare forwards the client's `Range` header to your origin. For `GET` requests over HTTPS, Cloudflare now also forwards the client's own `Accept-Encoding` header instead of Cloudflare's default `gzip, br` header. Previously, Cloudflare passed your origin's byte-range `206 Partial Content` response to the client without decoding it, so a client could receive a range in an encoding it did not accept.

If a client sends no `Accept-Encoding` header (on Orange-to-Orange requests), or sends only stripped dictionary encodings (`dcb` or `dcz`), your origin can receive an empty `Accept-Encoding` header. Under [RFC 9110, section 12.5.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-12.5.3), an empty `Accept-Encoding` header means the client accepts no encoding, so your origin should answer it with an unencoded response rather than `406 Not Acceptable`.

Range requests that Cloudflare serves from cache, or fetches with Origin Range Requests, still send Cloudflare's own `Accept-Encoding` header to your origin.

For more information, refer to [Range request behavior](/cache/reference/range-requests/).
